titleText.es: En el diagrama de ESdlA, arriba y abajo corresponden APROXIMADAMENTE a noroeste y sureste, respectivamente.
titleText.en: In the LotR map, up and down correspond LOOSELY to northwest and southeast respectively.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish text is the exact title attribute in the Spanish archive, and the English text is the exact official xkcd title attribute.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: On a diagram, líneas can refer to the drawn paths that trace people or things, rather than lines of written text.

example.es: Cada línea muestra una ruta distinta.
example.en: Each line shows a different route.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: For the body-part sense, lengua means “tongue.” In a separate sense, lengua can mean “language.”
Used as a noun, muertos names people who are dead. Spanish can use an adjective with a plural article understood from context to refer to a group of people.
Rumbo names the direction in which someone or something is traveling. With a, it commonly introduces the destination.
Ent is Tolkien's name for one of these beings; Spanish uses ents as the plural.

example.es: Los ents parecen árboles que caminan.
example.en: The Ents look like walking trees.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hobbit is a fantasy name used in Spanish; its plural is hobbits.

example.es: Los hobbits viven en la Comarca.
example.en: The hobbits live in the Shire.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Olifantes is the Spanish name for Tolkien's enormous elephant-like war animals.

example.en: The oliphaunts look like enormous elephants.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: on; against; introduces the target of an attack
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After ataque, a can introduce the person or thing being attacked.

example.es: El ataque al castillo empezó de noche.
example.en: The attack on the castle began at night.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Raptor can be used as a shortened dinosaur name; this sense does not refer to a bird of prey.

example.es: El raptor corre hacia la puerta.
example.en: The raptor runs toward the door.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; with comen, it emphasizes eating someone up
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Comer means 'to eat.' With a matching short word such as me, te, or se, comerse can emphasize eating something completely.

example.es: Los niños se comen el pastel.
example.en: The children eat up the cake.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something is heading toward a destination?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use rumbo a followed by the destination. Before el, a and el combine as al.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Rumbo means a course or heading, and a introduces the destination. The destination can be a place or a direction; only the form before el contracts, as in rumbo al norte.

example.es: El tren va rumbo a Sevilla.
example.en: The train is heading toward Seville.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: charts that turn a movie's character interactions into paths through time
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Each line follows a character, and nearby lines show characters sharing a scene. The joke contrasts stories that form readable patterns with Primer, whose famously tangled time-travel plot becomes an almost indecipherable knot.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: Jedi; relating to the Jedi Order
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish can use jedi as a noun or as an adjective after a noun; in adjective use, it describes something related to the Jedi Order.

example.es: El joven empezó su entrenamiento jedi.
example.en: The young man began his Jedi training.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Puerta can name a large defended gate as well as an ordinary door inside a building.

example.es: Cerraron la puerta de la fortaleza.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before el plus a masculine singular noun, todo means the whole amount or extent of it: todo el día, todo el trabajo.
Before a specific moment, en can correspond to English “at.”

example.en: He arrived at just the right moment.
